task_instance: Write and compile a minimal Android Application class that initializes the Zoom Contact Center SDK in Application.onCreate, builds a ZoomCCItem with an entryId, obtains a ZoomCCChatService, and releases the service on teardown, per the SKILL.md 'Hard Guardrails' section.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable requires linking against the proprietary Zoom Contact Center Android SDK (classes such as com.zoom.zoomcontactcenter.ZoomCCInterface, ZoomCCChatService, ZoomCCItem, ZoomCCVideoService, ZoomCCZVAService, ZoomCCScheduledCallbackService). This is a closed-source binary distributed only via Zoom's developer marketplace / private Maven repository (https://marketplacefront.zoom.us/sdk/contact/android/), which requires network access and a Zoom developer account/API key to obtain -- neither of which is available on this air-gapped machine. Searched the entire filesystem for any local copy of the SDK (aar/jar) and found none. Additionally, even the basic Android platform SDK is incomplete here: /usr/lib/android-sdk contains only build-tools, with no platforms/android.jar and no kotlinc, so genuine Android app code (even ignoring the Zoom SDK) cannot be compiled in this runtime at all. A curl test to the SDK's marketplace host was also blocked (403 from the proxy), confirming no network path exists. The SKILL.md's own linked reference files (concepts/sdk-lifecycle.md, examples/service-patterns.md, references/android-reference-map.md, troubleshooting/common-issues.md, RUNBOOK.md) are also absent from the local skill directory (only SKILL.md and LICENSE exist), so even the skill's own detailed guidance is unavailable offline.
evidence: Ran `which java javac gradle kotlinc android sdkmanager` -> only java/javac/gradle present, no kotlinc/android/sdkmanager. Ran `find / -iname android.jar` under /usr/lib/android-sdk -> no results (only build-tools/ present, no platforms/). Ran `find / -iname '*zoomcc*' -o -iname 'ZoomCCInterface*'` across the whole filesystem -> no matches; only unrelated 'zoom' hits (UI icon files, video-editor icons) turned up. Ran `curl -sS --max-time 3 https://marketplacefront.zoom.us` -> 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403', confirming no network egress to the SDK distribution host. Wrote a representative CCApplication.java implementing the skill's mandated lifecycle pattern (init in onCreate, ZoomCCItem/entryId, release on teardown) at src/main/java/com/example/cc/CCApplication.java with the real SDK calls commented out (since the classes do not exist locally). Attempted `javac` compilation of even the Android-framework parts (android.app.Application) and it failed with 'package android.app does not exist' / 'cannot find symbol: class Application', proving the environment cannot compile Android code at all, independent of the Zoom SDK gap. Confirmed benchmark/ce_sources_div/.../android/ directory contains only SKILL.md and LICENSE (no referenced sub-docs) via `ls -la`. No deliverable could be produced or verified; the task is blocked by the unavailable proprietary SDK plus an incomplete local Android toolchain, both requiring network access to remedy.
